dd.s1.criterion:
- All intended wires are gathered into a single parallel group with no strand crossing out or hanging free
- The bundle lies straight along its run with no visible bow or loop
- A tape measure is in place along the bundle with its zero end at the start of the run

sources.condition: The gathered bundle measures 1 inch or less in diameter at its largest point.
sources.note: Handbook: "single cord-lacing method and tying tape may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet repeats 1" limit.

sources.condition: All wires intended for the bundle are gathered as one parallel group with no strand crossing out or looping free.
sources.note: Sheet: "Gather the wires to be bundled together." Uniform bundle is prerequisite to valid length measurement.

sources.condition: Slack is pulled out of the wires before the tape is read, so the bundle lies straight and unbowed.
sources.note: Sheet: "Pull the slack out of the wires and use a tape measure to identify the distance." Tautness cannot be judged from a still.

sources.condition: A tape-measure reading of the bundle run length is obtained and recorded for the cord calculation.
sources.note: Sheet directs use of a tape measure; the recorded distance drives the 2x cord length in the next step.

not_photo_gradeable: Bundle diameter of 1 inch or less (requires a caliper or rule reading)
Slack actually pulled out of the wires before reading (tension judgement, seen only in the action)
The recorded length value used for cord calculation
dd.s1.required_framing: Two frames: one along the full bundle run with the tape measure laid beside it and the reading legible, and one across the bundle with a rule or caliper showing diameter.

dd.s2.step_text: Cut the required length of lacing cord.
dd.s2.criterion:
- A single continuous length of lacing cord, no splices or joining knots along it
- Both cut ends clean and square with no unravelled or frayed braid
- Cord free of kinks, dirt and contamination, coiled or laid out ready for use

sources.condition: The cut cord length equals twice the measured bundle distance (e.g., 4 ft bundle → 8 ft cord).
sources.note: Senior Mechanic Note 2: "Multiply the distance by 2. Cut that length of lacing cord." Handbook gives no cord-length figure.

sources.condition: The cord is one continuous piece with no splices, knots or joined segments.
sources.note: Single cord-lacing method requires one running cord for starting knot, hitches and finish knot.

sources.condition: The cord used is waxed lacing cord of the type listed for the task.
sources.note: Equipment list item 9: "Waxed lacing cord"; wax content and cord spec are read from spool label/spec, not appearance.

sources.condition: Cut ends are clean, with no unravelled or frayed strands of the braided cord.
sources.note: Workmanship implied by use of diagonal cutters and later requirement to inspect for "long strands."

not_photo_gradeable: Cut length equals twice the measured bundle distance (requires tape-measure reading)
Cord is the specified waxed lacing cord (established from spool label or spec)
dd.s2.required_framing: Lay the cut cord out full length beside an extended tape measure with the zero mark at one end, with both cut ends visible in frame; include the cord spool label if available.

ts.s1.section: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method
ts.s1.criterion:
- Start point is on a straight section of bundle with no clamp, connector, splice or breakout within the knot area
- Wires at the start point are gathered parallel and snug, with no crossed or protruding strands
- Surrounding hardware is visible in frame so the clearance of the chosen location can be judged

sources.condition: The chosen start point lies on a straight, unobstructed run of bundle, clear of clamps, connectors, splices and breakouts.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: "Start the lacing at a clear section of the bundle, free of obstacles." Handbook gives no locating requirement.

sources.condition: The gathered bundle at the start point measures 1 inch or less in diameter, qualifying it for single cord lacing.
sources.note: Handbook: "single cord-lacing method ... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet: "Must be 1” in diameter or less."

sources.condition: Wires are gathered parallel with slack pulled out at the start point, no crossed or protruding strands.
sources.note: Sheet: "Pull the slack out of the wires"; a clear start section requires the bundle be formed before knotting.

not_photo_gradeable: Bundle diameter of 1 inch or less at the start point (requires measurement)
Whether slack was actually pulled out of the wires before gathering (action, not visible in a still)
ts.s1.required_framing: One still showing roughly 12 inches of bundle centered on the selected start point, with adjacent clamps/connectors/breakouts visible in frame, plus a rule or caliper across the bundle if diameter is being documented.

ts.s2.section: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method
ts.s2.criterion:
- Cord passes completely around the back of the bundle and both ends emerge in front, forming a clear V
- Cord lies flat against the bundle with no twists or kinks visible
- All wires of the group are inside the wrap; none excluded or pinched
- Wrap is at a clear section of the bundle, free of clamps or obstacles

sources.condition: The short working tail extending from the bundle measures approximately 8 inches.
sources.note: Sheet note 2: "Pass about 8" of cord behind the bundle"; handbook gives no tail length.

sources.condition: The cord fully encircles the bundle behind it, with both ends emerging in front forming a V.
sources.note: Sheet note 2: "Pull the cord from both sides, making a V around the bundle."

sources.condition: The cord lies flat and untwisted against the bundle and no individual wire is excluded or pinched out of the group.
sources.note: Sheet note 1 of prior section: wires gathered with slack pulled out before lacing.

sources.condition: Both cord ends are drawn snug so no slack loop remains behind the bundle before the hitch is tied.
sources.note: Sheet note 2 requires pulling from both sides; slack behind the bundle is hidden in a still.

sources.condition: The bundle being laced is 1 inch or less in diameter, qualifying it for the single cord-lacing method.
sources.note: Handbook p.9-87: "single cord-lacing method ... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet: "Must be 1" in diameter or less."

not_photo_gradeable: Approximately 8 inches of tail cord (requires a measured length)
Snugness of the cord with no slack loop behind the bundle
Bundle diameter of 1 inch or less
ts.s2.required_framing: Shoot the bundle from the front at the starting position, the full V and both cord ends in frame, with a rule or tape laid alongside the short tail so its length reads.

ts.s3.section: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method
ts.s3.criterion:
- Two cord turns encircle the bundle with the working end crossing over the standing part and passing under the loop (clove hitch form)
- Turns lie flat and adjacent against the bundle, not crossed or stacked
- Cord seats on the bundle without pinching, denting or displacing wire insulation
- A short-strand tail remains free beyond the hitch for the securing knot

sources.condition: The knot shows two turns around the bundle with the working end crossing over and passing under the loop, forming a true clove hitch.
sources.note: Handbook Fig. 9-148 labels "Cord crosses under loop" and text: "a clove hitch secured by a double-looped overhand knot".

sources.condition: The hitch stays cinched to the bundle and does not slip or loosen when hand tension on the ends is released.
sources.note: Sheet: "Tightly cinch the hitch" and "Keep tension on the ends to avoid the knot from slipping"; handbook: "Starting knot tightened".

sources.condition: The bundle laced by this single-cord clove hitch measures 1 inch or less in diameter.
sources.note: Handbook: "single cord-lacing method ... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet: "Must be 1" in diameter or less."

sources.condition: Enough short-strand tail remains beyond the hitch to tie the following double-looped overhand knot.
sources.note: Sheet passes about 8" of cord behind the bundle so the short strand can complete the securing knot.

not_photo_gradeable: Whether the hitch is genuinely cinched tight and will not slip when tension is released
Bundle diameter of 1 inch or less
Constant tension maintained on both ends while cinching
ts.s3.required_framing: Close, square-on shot of the starting knot filling the frame, bundle running left-to-right, with both cord ends visible and the knot's crossing point unobstructed; include a rule or tape across the bundle diameter in the same shot.

ts.s4.section: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method
ts.s4.step_text: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot.
ts.s4.criterion:
- A clove hitch is visible with a double-looped overhand locking knot tied over it
- Four crossings of the short cord over the long cord are countable, running back toward the clove hitch
- Knot body sits flat against the bundle with no open loops or protruding bights
- Two trimmed tail ends are present, cleanly cut, with no frayed or unraveling cord
- Wire insulation adjacent to the knot shows no cut, nick, or scuff from the cutters

sources.condition: The starting knot shows a clove hitch locked by a double-looped overhand knot, not a bare hitch.
sources.note: Handbook: "recommended knot for starting the single cord-lacing method is a clove hitch secured by a double-looped overhand knot"; sheet steps 3-4.

sources.condition: The short cord crosses over the long cord four times, running back toward the clove hitch.
sources.note: Sheet note 4: "Cross the short cord over the long cord four times back towards the clove hitch"; handbook gives no count.

sources.condition: Clipped tail ends are no shorter than 3/8 inch beyond the finished knot.
sources.note: Figure 9-148 callout states "Trim to 3/8" minimum"; procedure sheet only says clip excess tail cord off.

sources.condition: Both ends were pulled taut so the finished knot cannot be slid or worked loose on the bundle.
sources.note: Sheet note 4: "Pull both ends until taut"; tautness and slip resistance require watching the pull, not a still.

not_photo_gradeable: Tails trimmed to 3/8 inch minimum (needs a dimension against a scale)
Cord pulled taut and knot secure against slipping on the bundle
ts.s4.required_framing: Close-up perpendicular to the bundle, starting knot centered and filling the frame, both trimmed tails and the adjacent wire insulation visible, with a ruler or scale laid beside the tails.
conflicts: Procedure sheet says cross the short cord over the long cord four times; handbook p.9-87/9-88 specifies a 'double-looped overhand knot' (two loops) with no crossing count — procedure sheet is operative.

th.s1.section: Tie a Hitch Along the Bundle
th.s1.criterion:
- Hitches are spaced at visibly equal intervals along the bundle
- No unsupported gap noticeably larger than the other gaps
- Hitches sit in line along one side of the bundle rather than wandering around it
- Bundle appears gathered and round, not splayed, between hitches

sources.condition: Each new hitch is positioned approximately 6 inches from the previous knot.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: 'An approximate 6" gap provides adequate support.' Handbook gives no spacing figure for intermediate half hitches.

sources.condition: Spacing between successive hitches is visibly uniform along the laced length.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: 'Maintain equal distance between each hitch for uniformity and security.'

sources.condition: The cord run is held taut to the new hitch location with no slack or sag between knots.
sources.note: Procedure sheet: 'Start the hitch 1" from the end of your hand by pulling the cord taut to that spot.' Tension cannot be judged from a still.

sources.condition: Bundle being laced is 1 inch in diameter or less, suiting single cord-lacing.

Bundle diameter 1 inch or less (needs measurement)

th.s2.criterion:
- The knot is a half hitch: cord end visibly crosses over the run and passes back under the loop

- The run passes outside the bundle, with no cord pulled between individual wires or across a terminal/connector
- All hitches and the run line up along one side of the bundle, no crossed or doubled cord
- No frayed or splayed cord along the run

tf.s1.section: Tie a Finishing Knnot on a Bundle

- Preceding hitches remain aligned in a single row along the bundle

task.criterion:
- The bundle laced by the single cord-lacing method measures 1 inch or less in diameter at its largest point, confirmed by a legible instrument reading.
- The starting knot is a clove hitch secured by a double-looped overhand knot, with two turns visible and four over-under crossings countable, not a bare hitch.
- The finishing knot shows the cord wrapped twice around the bundle, the end crossing over the previous run and passing under its own loop, locked by four over-and-under passes running back toward the knot.
- All intermediate knots are half hitches lying in a single straight line on one side of the bundle, with no knot twisted off the row.
- Gaps between successive hitches are uniform end to end at approximately 6 inches (campus procedure figure).
- The lacing run between hitches lies straight along the bundle axis, flat against the bundle, not spiralled, not crossing other lacing, and not pulled down between individual wires or over a terminal or connector.
- Cord tails at both end knots are trimmed and retain at least 3/8 inch beyond the knot.
- No wire insulation near the clipped tails is nicked, cut, or scored.
- The cord used is a single continuous length of waxed lacing cord with no splices, cut to twice the measured bundle run (campus procedure).
- Every hitch resists being slid along the bundle or lifted into a slack loop by hand, verified by the witnessed pull/slide check.

sources.note: "The single cord-lacing method and tying tape may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less."

sources.condition: Starting knot is clove hitch plus double-looped overhand
sources.note: "the recommended knot for starting the single cord-lacing method is a clove hitch secured by a double-looped overhand knot."

sources.condition: Tail trimmed to at least 3/8 inch
sources.note: Figure callout reads "Trim to 3/8\" minimum"; machine-extracted figure text, PDF remains authority.
